problem: Existing audio-visual navigation (AVN, SoundSpaces, AV-WaN, SAVi) assumes an acoustically clean environment containing only the target sound, so agents fail when distracting or intentionally interfering sounds are present.
motivation: Real homes contain non-target sounds (children playing, people chatting), and an agent trained in clean settings becomes disabled when they appear. The paper builds an adversarial acoustic environment so the agent learns robust navigation, and finds that training under attack also transfers back to clean environments.
key_idea: Add a movable sound attacker that controls its position, volume and sound category in a zero-sum two-player game with the navigating agent, and train both jointly with a centralized critic and decentralized actors (PPO) so the agent becomes robust to sound interference.
insight: Training against a learned attacker improves not only robustness under attack but also clean-environment performance (SPL 0.742 vs 0.721 for AVN on Replica). Simply making the attacker louder is not better (volume 0.5 performed worse than 0.1 or 0.9), which justifies a learnable attacker. Independent training of agent and attacker fails to converge, while joint training converges (training curves). The attacker's power is bounded by a volume ratio, and the theory shows the attacker's perturbation lies in a sphere of radius epsilon.
method: Two-player zero-sum Markov game: the agent reward is r and the attacker reward is -r. The agent maximizes while the attacker minimizes the return, with value-decomposition-style joint return G=[G(agent), G(attacker)].

Sound attacker with hybrid action space: position (move forward/turn left/turn right/stop, like the agent), volume (11 discrete levels 0.0-1.0, bounded relative to the target sound) and category (101 SoundSpaces sounds). Its sound is convolved with the binaural RIR so it is physically realistic. The attacker is an invisible ghost with no collisions.

Agent and attacker networks: each has its own CNN encoders for RGB-D and the binaural spectrogram, concatenated into a GRU state, with linear actor-critic heads. The attacker has three heads (pos/vol/cat), each with an actor and a critic.
Joint training: a single PPO loss L = 1/2 L_agent + 1/6 (L_pos + L_vol + L_cat), following a centralized critic with decentralized actors, which converges, whereas independent learning does not.

Theory: Theorem 1 uses the linearity and convolution properties of the Fourier transform to show the attacker's observation perturbation (distance Δ in the STFT domain) is bounded by α·e/2π=ε, i.e. lies within an ε-sphere.
Attacker variants: SAAVN:P, V, C and PVC, where each attribute is either learned or fixed/random. The SA-MDP baseline is adapted to perturb only the audio input.

setting.backbone: ResNet-style CNN visual and audio encoders + GRU + actor-critic heads (trained from scratch with PPO)
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces episodes on Replica (0.1M training episodes, 30M agent steps) and Matterport3D (2M episodes, 60M steps), with 101 SoundSpaces sounds for the attacker; no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + binaural audio spectrogram (65x65x2 Replica / 65x26x2 MP3D)
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveForward, TurnLeft, TurnRight, Stop on a navigability graph (agent); attacker has hybrid position/volume/category actions
setting.privileged: none for the agent (the attacker's policy is used only in training/testing environment construction)

numbers.extra: trained under adversarial attacker, tested in clean environment; averaged over 5 runs

numbers_note: SoundSpaces AudioGoal is not in the canonical list, so it is labeled as SoundSpaces; SPL and SR are converted from the printed fractions to percentages. Several results (attack-strength curves, training curves) appear only in figures. Split naming: the paper reports 1000 test episodes, and 'test' is used for them.
results: SAAVN beats AVN in clean and attacked environments on both Replica and Matterport3D. On Replica clean, SPL is 0.742 vs 0.721 for AVN. Under the PVC attacker on Matterport3D, SPL is 0.478 vs 0.397 for AVN. SA-MDP (audio-perturbation adaptation) is much worse than AVN.
limitations: Only one sound attacker is considered; multiple attackers are not studied.
Evaluated only in simulation; no real-robot tests, and the attacker is an invisible, non-colliding ghost.
Reporting is limited to SPL and mean reward in the main text, with many attacker variants and no standard-benchmark comparison against the newer AV-WaN/SAVi.
